source.title: Relative representations enable zero-shot latent space communication
source.authors: Luca Moschella; Valentino Maiorca; Marco Fumero; Antonio Norelli; Francesco Locatello; E. Rodolà

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some table layouts are ambiguous in the extracted text; those results are noted as left out.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests representational compatibility and zero-shot communication using relative representations and stitching, rather than testing scale-dependent convergence with the original claim’s method.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results on seed-to-seed geometry, cross-model relative similarities, and zero-shot stitching bear on V3, V4, V6, and partially V7. Cited findings from other work are excluded. Results comparing training-time classification performance of relative and absolute representations are not rows because they do not measure representational alignment. Results from Table 3 and Table 6 are left out because the extracted table layout does not reliably assign all values to their dataset/model conditions.
record.test_reason: The paper's own results bear on V3 and V4. On V3, distinct seed trainings give latent spaces with preserved angles, and seed-to-seed relative stitching works (Table 3). On V4, relative representations map independently trained word embeddings, language-specific RoBERTas, and BERT/ELECTRA/RoBERTa onto each other for zero-shot stitching. It uses a different method from the originals (anchor-based cosine representations, not CKA/mutual-kNN or unit matching). The Cora sweep (Fig. 3) also links model performance to similarity with a reference model, which bears weakly on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors conclude that latent spaces from different trainings differ by roughly angle-preserving transformations. Cosine-to-anchor relative representations remove this, enabling zero-shot stitching and comparison across seeds, architectures, languages and datasets. They validate on images, text and graphs, but do not stitch across modalities. They flag the similarity function and anchor choice and number as open questions.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs representations from cosine similarities to anchors and evaluates zero-shot stitching; it does not reproduce the original sources' convergence measurements or test convergence as a function of scale.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured distance changes when cosine similarity is replaced with vector-quantized similarity and as the quantization threshold changes (Figure 7). The paper also reports that stitching performance varies across languages and anchor sources (Table 4).

fits_no_version.finding: Vector-quantized similarity functions make FastText and Word2Vec relative spaces more similar than cosine relative spaces (score 1.24 down to 1.02; absolute 3.30).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The choice of invariance built into a relative representation changes how aligned two embedding spaces appear.

record.code_released: The paper says it releases a codebase, but no URL is stated in the text.
record.problems: The study does not test model scale or capability. Several conclusions rely on task performance as an indirect test of latent communication rather than a direct general-purpose alignment measure. The reported cross-language and cross-architecture stitching scores are incomplete and vary by condition. Some extracted table layouts, including Tables 3 and 6, do not support reliable assignment of every displayed value.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 stitching MSE results and Table 6 image stitching results were left out because the extracted layout does not unambiguously map all values to datasets, representation types, and model pairs. Appendix Tables 7–8 report multiple anchor-selection results; these were not extracted individually. Additional language and image results in Tables 15–18 were also left out to retain the clearest main-text results.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size and no comparison across independently trained models with different objectives or data as scale rises. Only the Cora performance–similarity correlation, against one reference model, touches it.
No vision–language alignment on paired images and captions.
Whether the same individual units, features or subspaces recur. Only global angle preservation and stitching are shown.
No interpretable feature, neuron or circuit matching.
No comparison of convergence measures or kNN settings for measuring alignment, and no OOD test of convergence. The metric rows are the study's own method variants.
Plateau with scale and causes of alignment (shared data or objectives) are not tested.

missing.what: Seed-to-seed zero-shot stitching MSE for AE/VAE, absolute vs relative, non-stitched vs stitched (e.g. MNIST AE relative 1.18 vs 2.83; absolute 0.66 vs 97.79)
Performance–similarity correlation across about 2000 Cora models against a reference (Pearson 0.955)
Cross-architecture image encoder stitching, ViT variants and RexNet, relative vs absolute (e.g. rexnet decoder with ViT encoders 53–60 vs 80 non-stitched)
CIFAR-10 ViT-base vs ViT-small relative similarity: Jaccard 0.11, MRR 0.27–0.39, cosine 0.96–0.97
All language-pair cross-lingual stitching (coarse and fine), and XLM-R, where relative stitching underperforms absolute
Anchor selection strategies changing word-embedding alignment (e.g. kmeans Jaccard 0.27, MRR 0.84 vs uniform 0.34, 0.94)

record.verdict_notes: Lang-9 to lang-12 are fabricated duplicates and should be deleted. The arch rows aggregate over model pairs. Absolute-stitching rows are controls, not V4 tests. The V1 label is weak: it rests on correlation with one reference in a single-dataset hyperparameter sweep. The study assumes convergence (it cites it in related work) while also measuring it.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size or capability, and no test of whether cross-model alignment rises with scale.
No vision-language comparison on paired images and captions.
The paper reports angle preservation across trainings, but does not test whether the same individual features, neurons, or shared subspaces recur.
Tests relative representations and zero-shot stitching; does not test every listed mapping approach, such as layer stitching, or establish that all mappings work without paired anchors.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Tests cosine versus vector-quantized similarity for one embedding comparison. It does not systematically test out-of-distribution inputs or whether convergence vanishes under other reasonable measures.

Some similarity scores and stitching results are incomplete rather than perfect. The paper does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, or whether alignment plateaus with scale.

relationships.condition: Same AE/VAE architecture on MNIST and other image datasets, different seeds
relationships.reason: Seed-1 shows latent angles preserved across seeds (figure only). The text's Table 3 shows relative seed-to-seed stitching MSE close to non-stitched (e.g. MNIST 2.83 vs 1.18), against about 98 for absolute.
relationships.display_finding: Latent angles were preserved across seeds, and MNIST relative-stitching MSE was 2.83 versus 1.18 without stitching and about 98 with absolute stitching.
